translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on wuchen, he visited the Prince of Jin's residence to view the new pool.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, on wuchen in the seventh month, he called at the Prince of Jin's house to see the new pool.

sentences.zh: 丙子，幸京兆尹光美第視疾。

translations.literal: On bingzi, he visited the residence of the Metropolitan Governor Guangyi to see him in illness.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi he went to Metropolitan Governor Guangyi's home to inquire after his illness.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，再幸光美第。

translations.literal: On wuyin, he again visited Guangyi's residence.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin he called on Guangyi again.

sentences.zh: 泉州節度使陳洪進乞朝覲。

translations.literal: Quanzhou military commissioner Chen Hongjin asked leave to attend court.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hongjin, commissioner of Quanzhou, petitioned to come to court.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，命近臣祈晴。

translations.literal: On bingxu, close ministers were ordered to pray for clear weather.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu he sent his intimates to pray for fair skies.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，命修先代帝王及五嶽四瀆祠廟。

translations.literal: On dinghai, repair was ordered for the temples of former dynasties' emperors and of the Five Sacred Peaks and Four Rivers.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai he ordered the shrines of ancient emperors and of the Five Peaks and Four Rivers restored.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，幸光美第。

translations.literal: On gengyin, he visited Guangyi's residence.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin he visited Guangyi again.

sentences.zh: 八月乙未朔，吳越國王進射火箭軍士。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the yiwei new moon, the king of Wuyue presented rocket archers.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiwei new moon of the eighth month Qian Chu sent companies trained in fire-arrows.

sentences.zh: 己亥，幸新龍興寺。

translations.literal: On jihai, he visited the new Longxing Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai he toured the new Longxing Temple.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，太子中允郭思齊坐贓棄市。

translations.literal: On xinchou, Palace Attendant Guo Siqi, for taking bribes, was executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou Palace Attendant Guo Siqi was beheaded in the market for corruption.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，幸等覺院，遂幸東染院，賜工人錢。

translations.literal: On yisi, he visited Dengjue Cloister, then visited the Eastern Dye Works and bestowed money on the laborers.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi he went to Dengjue Cloister, then to the Eastern Dye Works and paid the workers in cash.

sentences.zh: 又幸控鶴營觀習射，賜帛有差。

translations.literal: He again visited the Crane-Control Camp to watch archery practice and bestowed silks in graded measure.
translations.idiomatic: He called next at the Crane-Control Camp for an archery drill and gave graded gifts of silk.

sentences.zh: 又幸開寶寺觀藏經。

translations.literal: He again visited Kaibao Temple to view the sutra repository.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to Kaibao Temple to inspect the scripture library.

sentences.zh: 丁未，遣侍衛馬軍都指揮使党進、宣徽北院使潘美伐北漢。

translations.literal: On dingwei, Palace Cavalry commander Dang Jin and Northern Court commissioner Pan Mei were dispatched to attack Northern Han.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei he sent Palace Cavalry commander Dang Jin and Northern Court commissioner Pan Mei against Northern Han.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，遣使率兵分五道入太原。

translations.literal: On bingchen, envoys were dispatched to lead troops in five columns into Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen he sent armies in five divisions against Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 九月甲子，幸綾錦院。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on jiazi, he visited the Brocade Office.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi in the ninth month he toured the Brocade Office.

sentences.zh: 庚午，權高麗國事王伷遣使來朝獻。

translations.literal: On gengwu, Wang Xiu, acting ruler of Goryeo, sent envoys to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu Wang Xiu, regent of Goryeo, sent envoys to present tribute.

sentences.zh: 党進敗北漢軍於太原城北。

translations.literal: Dang Jin defeated Northern Han troops north of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Dang Jin routed the Northern Han army north of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，命忻、代行營都監郭進遷山後諸州民。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Guo Jin, chief inspector of the Xing and Dai field headquarters, was ordered to relocate the people of the prefectures beyond the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi Guo Jin, overseer of the Xing-Dai front, was told to move the populace of the hill country.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，幸城南池亭，遂幸禮賢宅，又幸晉王第。

translations.literal: On gengyin, he visited the pool pavilion south of the city, then visited the Lodge for Honoring the Worthy, and again visited the Prince of Jin's residence.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin he went to the southern pool pavilion, then to the Lodge for Honoring the Worthy, and finally to the Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 帝性孝友節儉，質任自然，不事矯飾。

translations.literal: The emperor by nature was filial, brotherly, and frugal; plain and trusting in what was natural, he did not indulge in affectation.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was filial toward his kin, fond of his brothers, and spare in habit—plain, trusting nature, and free of show.

sentences.zh: 受禪之初，頗好微行，或諫其輕出。

translations.literal: At the beginning of his receiving the Mandate he rather liked going out incognito, and some remonstrated that he went forth too lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Early in his reign he often slipped out in disguise, and counselors warned that he courted danger.

sentences.zh: 曰：「帝王之興，自有天命，周世宗見諸將方面大耳者皆殺之，我終日侍側，不能害也。

translations.literal: He said, "The rise of an emperor has its own Heaven-appointed destiny. Emperor Shizong of Zhou saw generals with large ears in every quarter and killed them; I attended him all day at his side, yet he could not harm me."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Heaven chooses its emperors. Zhou Shizong used to kill every commander with prominent ears; I stood at his side all day, and he never touched me."

sentences.zh: 」既而微行愈數，有諫，輒語之曰：「有天命者任自為之，不汝禁也。

translations.literal: Presently his incognito outings grew more frequent; when there was remonstrance he would tell them, "Whoever has the Mandate may do as he pleases—I shall not forbid you."
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was slipping out even more often; when advisers protested he would say, "Let Heaven's chosen walk free—you need not stop me."

sentences.zh: 」一日，罷朝，坐便殿，不樂者久之。

translations.literal: One day, after court was dismissed, he sat in the side hall, unhappy for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: One day, when court had ended, he lingered in the side hall, long out of sorts.

sentences.zh: 左右請其故。

translations.literal: Those at his side asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants asked what weighed on him.

sentences.zh: 曰：「爾謂為天子容易耶？

translations.literal: He said, "Do you think being Son of Heaven is easy?"
translations.idiomatic: "You think wearing the crown is easy?" he said.

sentences.zh: 早作乘快誤決一事，故不樂耳。

translations.literal: I rose early and rode fast and decided one matter wrongly, and that is why I am unhappy."
translations.idiomatic: "I was up before dawn, rode hard, and still botched a judgment—that is all."

sentences.zh: 」汴京新宮成，御正殿坐，令洞開諸門，謂左右曰：「此如我心，少有邪曲，人皆見之。」

translations.literal: When the new palace at Bianjing was completed, he sat in the main hall with all the gates thrown open and told those at his side, "This is like my heart—if there is the least crookedness within, everyone can see it."
translations.idiomatic: When the new Bian capital palace stood finished, he took the main throne with every gate flung wide and said, "My heart is this hall—bend it inward even slightly, and the world looks straight through."

sentences.zh: 吳越錢俶來朝，自宰相以下咸請留俶而取其地，帝不聽，遣俶歸國。

translations.literal: When Qian Chu of Wuyue came to court, from the chief councilors down all asked that Chu be detained and his territory taken; the emperor would not listen and sent Chu home to his state.
translations.idiomatic: When Qian Chu of Wuyue arrived, every minister from the chief councilor down urged that he be held and his lands seized; Taizu refused and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 及辭，取群臣留俶章疏數十軸，封識遺俶，戒以途中密觀，俶屆途啟視，皆留己不遣之章也。

translations.literal: At his farewell the emperor took several tens of rolls of memorials from the ministers asking that Chu be detained, sealed and labeled them, and left them with Chu, admonishing him to read them secretly on the road; when Chu opened them on the journey, every memorial was one that had asked to keep him and not let him go.
translations.idiomatic: At parting he handed Chu a bundle of dozens of sealed memorials urging detention, telling him to read them privately on the road; every sheet inside had pleaded to keep Chu at court.

sentences.zh: 俶自是感懼，江南平，遂乞納土。

translations.literal: From this Chu was moved to fear; when Jiangnan was pacified, he begged to surrender his territory.
translations.idiomatic: Chu left terrified; after Jiangnan fell he offered to surrender his kingdom.

sentences.zh: 南漢劉鋹在其國，好置酖以毒臣下。

translations.literal: Liu Chang of Southern Han, while still in his own state, was fond of setting poisoned wine to kill his ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chang of Southern Han had made a habit at home of poisoning ministers who displeased him.

sentences.zh: 既歸朝，從幸講武池，帝酌卮酒賜鋹，鋹疑有毒，捧杯泣曰：「臣罪在不赦，陛下既待臣以不死，願為大梁布衣，觀太平之盛，未敢飲此酒。

translations.literal: After he had submitted to the court, while accompanying the emperor at the Lecture-on-Military-Affairs Pool the emperor poured a cup of wine and bestowed it on Chang; Chang suspected poison, held the cup and wept, saying, "My crime admits no pardon, yet Your Majesty has treated me as one not to die—I beg to be a commoner of Great Liang and witness the age of peace; I dare not drink this wine."
translations.idiomatic: Once at court, at the Lecture Pool Taizu filled a cup for him; Liu Chang, fearing poison, clutched it and wept: "I deserve death, yet you spared me—let me live out my days as a commoner of the dynasty and see the peace; I dare not drink."

sentences.zh: 」帝笑而謂之曰：「朕推赤心於人腹中，寧肯爾耶？

translations.literal: The emperor smiled and said to him, "I set my red heart in men's bellies—would I do such a thing to you?"
translations.idiomatic: Taizu laughed: "I lay my heart open in men's breasts—would I play you false?"

sentences.zh: 」即取鋹酒自飲，別酌以賜鋹。

translations.literal: Thereupon he took Chang's cup and drank it himself, then poured another cup and bestowed it on Chang.
translations.idiomatic: He drank Liu Chang's cup himself, then poured a fresh one and gave it to him.

sentences.zh: 王彥升擅殺韓通，雖預佐命，終身不與節鉞。

translations.literal: Wang Yansheng had killed Han Tong on his own authority; though he had shared in establishing the mandate, throughout his life he was never given a military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yansheng had murdered Han Tong without warrant; though he had helped win the throne, he never received a field command.

sentences.zh: 王全斌入蜀，貪恣殺降，雖有大功，即加貶絀。

translations.literal: Wang Quanbin entered Shu, was greedy and willful and killed those who surrendered; though he had great merit, he was at once demoted and fined.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Quanbin, conqueror of Shu, had looted and slaughtered captives; despite his victories he was stripped and fined at once.

sentences.zh: 宮中葦簾，緣用青布；

translations.literal: Reed curtains in the palace had their edges bound with blue cloth;
translations.idiomatic: Palace reed screens were edged with plain blue cloth;

sentences.zh: 常服之衣，浣濯至再。

translations.literal: everyday garments were washed and worn again.
translations.idiomatic: and everyday robes were washed and worn a second time.

sentences.zh: 魏國長公主襦飾翠羽，戒勿復用，又教之曰：「汝生長富貴，當念惜福。

translations.literal: The Princess of Wei wore a jacket ornamented with kingfisher feathers; he admonished her not to use it again and also taught her, saying, "You were born to wealth and honor—you must think to cherish your blessing."
translations.idiomatic: When the Princess of Wei appeared in a jacket trimmed with kingfisher feathers he forbade it and told her, "You were born to privilege—learn to husband your fortune."

sentences.zh: 」見孟昶寶裝溺器，摏而碎之，曰：「汝以七寶飾此，當以何器貯食？

translations.literal: Seeing Meng Chang's urinal adorned with jewels, he smashed it and said, "You ornament this with the seven treasures—what vessel will you use to hold food?"
translations.idiomatic: He shattered Meng Chang's jewel-encrusted chamber pot and cried, "If you gild a piss-pot with the seven treasures, what bowl is left for your rice?"

sentences.zh: 所為如是，不亡何待！」

translations.literal: Conduct like this—if you do not perish, what are you waiting for!"
translations.idiomatic: "Men who live like that do not wait long to fall."

sentences.zh: 晚好讀書，嘗讀二典，歎曰：「堯、舜之罪四凶，止從投竄，何近代法網之密乎！

translations.literal: In his later years he loved reading books; once reading the two canons, he sighed and said, "Yao and Shun punished the four villains only by banishing them—how dense the net of recent ages has become!"
translations.idiomatic: Late in life he took to books; reading the canons of Yao and Shun he sighed, "Those sages punished the four criminals with exile alone—how tight our laws have grown since!"

sentences.zh: 」謂宰相曰：「五代諸侯跋扈，有枉法殺人者，朝廷置而不問。

translations.literal: He told the chief councilors, "In the Five Dynasties the military governors were overbearing; some killed men in violation of law, yet the court set the matter aside and did not inquire."
translations.idiomatic: He told his councilors, "Under the Five Dynasties warlords murdered at will and the throne looked away."

sentences.zh: 人命至重，姑息藩鎮，當若是耶？

translations.literal: Human life is of the utmost weight—should one indulge the military governors like that?"
translations.idiomatic: "Life is the heaviest thing under Heaven—are we to coddle warlords still?"

sentences.zh: 自今諸州決大辟，錄案聞奏，付刑部覆視之。

translations.literal: From now on, wherever a prefecture passes sentence of death, the case record shall be memorialized to the throne and submitted to the Ministry of Justice for review."
translations.idiomatic: "Henceforth every capital sentence in the provinces must be filed to court and reviewed by the Ministry of Justice."

sentences.zh: 」遂著為令。

translations.literal: This was thereupon written into statute.
translations.idiomatic: The rule was entered into law.

sentences.zh: 乾德改元，先諭宰相曰：「年號須擇前代所未有者。

translations.literal: When the Qian De era name was changed, he first instructed the chief councilors, "The reign title must be chosen from among those no former age has used."
translations.idiomatic: When he chose the era name Qian De he told the councilors, "Pick a reign title no dynasty has used before."

sentences.zh: 」三年，蜀平，蜀宮人入內，帝見其鏡背有志「乾德四年鑄」者，召竇儀等詰之。

translations.literal: In year three, when Shu was pacified, Shu palace women entered the inner quarters; the emperor saw on the back of a mirror an inscription reading "Cast in the fourth year of Qian De," and summoned Dou Yi and others to question them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, after Shu fell, its palace women entered the harem; on a mirror's back he read "Cast Qian De year four" and summoned Dou Yi and the scholars to explain.

sentences.zh: 儀對曰：「此必蜀物，蜀主嘗有此號。

translations.literal: Yi replied, "This must be a Shu object; the Shu ruler once used this era name."
translations.idiomatic: Dou Yi answered, "It is surely a Shu piece—the Shu king once took that era name."

sentences.zh: 」乃大喜曰：「作相須讀書人。

translations.literal: Thereupon he said in great delight, "To be chief councilor one must be a man of reading."
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, he said, "A chief councilor must be a man who has read books."

sentences.zh: 」由是大重儒者。

translations.literal: From this he greatly valued the Confucian literati.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he held the scholar-officials in high regard.

sentences.zh: 受命杜太后，傳位太宗。

translations.literal: He received the mandate from Empress Dowager Du and transmitted the throne to Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: He took the throne at Empress Dowager Du's charge and passed it to Taizong.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗病亟，帝往視之，親為灼艾，太宗覺痛，帝亦取艾自灸。

translations.literal: When Taizong once lay gravely ill, the emperor went to see him and personally performed moxibustion on him; when Taizong felt pain, the emperor also took moxa and cauterized himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong fell deathly ill Taizu tended him and burned moxa into his skin; feeling the prince's pain, he burned his own flesh as well.

sentences.zh: 每對近臣言：太宗龍行虎步，生時有異，他日必為太平天子，福德吾所不及云。

translations.literal: He often told close ministers that Taizong walked like a dragon and tiger, had strangeness at birth, and would one day certainly become the Son of Heaven who brings great peace—his own fortune could not match it, he said.
translations.idiomatic: He often told intimates that Taizong moved like dragon and tiger, bore signs at birth, and would surely become the peaceful emperor—fortune his elder brother could not equal.

sentences.zh: 讚曰：昔者堯、舜以禪代，湯、武以征伐，皆南面而有天下。

translations.literal: Eulogy: In antiquity Yao and Shun yielded the throne by abdication; Tang and Wu took it by punitive expedition—each faced south and possessed all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Eulogy: Yao and Shun received the realm through abdication; Tang and Wu through war—each turned south and ruled the world.

sentences.zh: 四聖人者往，世道升降，否泰推移。

translations.literal: When the four sages had gone, the way of the world rose and fell, and prosperity and adversity shifted in turn.
translations.idiomatic: After those four sages passed, fortune and ruin traded places through the ages.

sentences.zh: 當斯民塗炭之秋，皇天眷求民主，亦惟責其濟斯世而已。

translations.literal: In the season when the people were scorched and charred, High Heaven in its care sought a lord for the people, charging only that he rescue this age.
translations.idiomatic: When the people lay in ashes Heaven looked for a ruler for them, asking only that he save the age.

sentences.zh: 使其必得四聖人之才，而後以其行事畀之，則生民平治之期，殆無日也。

translations.literal: Had one insisted on finding men equal to the four sages in talent before committing the task to them, the day when the people would know good order would scarcely ever have come.
translations.idiomatic: Wait until men equal to those four appear before entrusting the age, and the people may never see peace.

sentences.zh: 五季亂極，宋太祖起介胄之中，踐九五之位，原其得國，視晉、漢、周亦豈甚相絕哉？

translations.literal: When disorder in the Five Dynasties reached its extreme, Song Taizu rose from within armor and tread the throne of the Nine and Five; considering how he gained the state, was he so very far removed from Jin, Han, and Zhou?
translations.idiomatic: From the chaos of the Five Dynasties Taizu rose in mail to the throne; judged by how he won the realm, he differed little from the Jin, Han, or Zhou founders.

sentences.zh: 及其發號施令，名藩大將，俯首聽命，四方列國，次第削平，此非人力所易致也。

translations.literal: Yet when he issued orders and commands, famous circuits and great generals bowed their heads in obedience, and the states of the four quarters were in sequence cut down and pacified—this was not something human effort alone could easily bring about.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when he commanded, great warlords bowed, and kingdom after kingdom fell—no mere human effort explains it.

sentences.zh: 建隆以來，釋藩鎮兵權，繩贓吏重法，以塞濁亂之源。

translations.literal: From the Jianlong era onward he loosened the military governors' grip on troops, bound corrupt officials with heavy law, and blocked the sources of turbid disorder.
translations.idiomatic: From Jianlong on he stripped the governors of their armies, tightened the law on venal officials, and choked off the springs of disorder.

sentences.zh: 州郡司牧，下至令錄、幕職，躬自引對；

translations.literal: Prefectural and circuit governors, down to magistrates, assistants, and staff officers, he personally summoned for audience;
translations.idiomatic: He summoned every prefect, circuit intendant, magistrate, aide, and clerk to audience himself;

sentences.zh: 務農興學，慎罰薄斂，與世休息，迄於丕平；

translations.literal: he promoted farming and encouraged learning, was cautious in punishment and light in exaction, and rested the age until great peace was achieved;
translations.idiomatic: promoted tillage and schools, punished sparingly and taxed lightly, and let the realm breathe until peace held firm;

sentences.zh: 治定功成，制禮作樂。

translations.literal: when order was settled and the work accomplished, he regulated ritual and made music.
translations.idiomatic: and when order stood firm he set ritual and composed music.

sentences.zh: 在位十有七年之間，而三百餘載之基，傳之子孫，世有典則。

translations.literal: In the seventeen years of his reign he laid a foundation of more than three hundred years, transmitted to sons and grandsons with institutions for every generation.
translations.idiomatic: In seventeen years on the throne he laid a foundation that would last three centuries, passing laws and precedent to sons and grandsons.

sentences.zh: 遂使三代而降，考論聲明文物之治，道德仁義之風，宋於漢、唐，蓋無讓焉。

translations.literal: Thus from the Three Dynasties downward, in weighing civilized government, cultural achievement, and the wind of moral benevolence, Song yields nothing to Han and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Three Dynasties, in culture, ritual, and the breath of humane rule, Song stands even with Han and Tang.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，創業垂統之君，規模若是，亦可謂遠也已矣！

translations.literal: Alas, for a founding emperor who bequeaths a lasting pattern—if his scale was such, it may be called far-reaching indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Alas—a founder who sets the pattern for ages on such a scale may truly be called far-seeing.
